thread:
jamie (Support): Heads up — customer hitting 400 on POST /v1/rerank. Error says \"invalid request: items must be a non-empty array\". They attached the body and say it used to work yesterday.
eli (Client Eng): can you paste the exact body they sent? sometimes client SDKs wrap arrays in an object or send nulls.
jamie (Support): pasted below (from customer):
```
{
  "model": "redwood/rerank-l1",
  "items": null,
  "queries": ["Which article is best?"],
  "top_k": 3
}
```
eli (Client Eng): aha — items is null. That would trigger our schema validation. Also top_k should be numeric not string but here it's fine. Did they batch multiple requests?
devx-bot: New ticket created: CS-1289 — assigned to @eli.
maria (SRE): FYI sometimes the iOS client transforms empty lists to null when serializing — we've seen this on older SDKs.
eli (Client Eng): repro steps I used: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @payload.json (payload above). Response: 400 {\"error\":\"invalid request: items must be array of candidates\"} 
jamie (Support): customer says they call through our JS SDK v2.3.4 — I'll ask them to dump the raw network body.
eli (Client Eng): temporary workaround: validate before sending and replace null items with [] and include candidate objects: [{"id":"c1","text":"...","score":0}]. Also add server-side defensive check to return clearer error: HTTP 400 with field path. I'll open a small PR to improve error message.
maria (SRE): note — if items=[] we still reject (empty array) per rerank contract. We should log clearer telemetry so Support can map to SDK versions.
jamie (Support): pinging customer with repro and workaround. Will ask for SDK version & a HAR file. :thumbsup:
eli (Client Eng): thx — if they repro with the raw curl and still get 400, escalate and include the exact response body, headers, and a minimal reproducible payload.
jamie (Support): update: customer returned HAR and indeed the client serialized items as the string "null". Sent them a code snippet to sanitize: `if (!Array.isArray(body.items)) body.items = []` and asked them to retry.
eli (Client Eng): marking as likely client serialization bug. I'll follow up on the SDK changelog to add a guard.
jamie (Support): closing loop with customer once they confirm.
